description: This course introduces the design, implementation and analysis of efficient algorithms. Students learn algorithmic paradigms such as divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy methods, backtracking and graph algorithms along with suitable data structures for solving computational problems.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Concept of time and space complexity, analysis of algorithms, asymptotic notation, recurrence relations, divide-and-conquer algorithms, Quick Sort, Heap Sort, priority queues, linear-time sorting algorithms, hashing and binary search trees.

syllabus.title: Graph Algorithms
syllabus.body: Graph representation and traversal, graph search, topological sorting, strongly connected components, minimum spanning trees using Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, single-source shortest paths, relaxation, Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford algorithm, shortest paths in directed acyclic graphs and all-pairs shortest path algorithms.

syllabus.title: B-Trees and Dynamic Programming
syllabus.body: Representation and operations of B-Trees, fundamentals of dynamic programming, stages of dynamic programming, matrix-chain multiplication and longest common subsequence.

syllabus.title: Greedy and Backtracking Algorithms
syllabus.body: Greedy strategy, activity selection problem, Huffman coding, task scheduling, knapsack problem, backtracking, 8-Queens problem, graph coloring and Hamiltonian cycle.

outcomes: Design, implement and analyze searching and sorting algorithms.
Apply divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy and backtracking techniques to solve computational problems.
Select appropriate data structures such as heaps, trees and hashing for efficient algorithm design.
Implement graph algorithms including shortest path, minimum spanning tree and topological sorting.
Analyze algorithm complexity using asymptotic notations and recurrence relations.
textbooks: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest and Clifford Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd Edition, PHI.
Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni and Sanguthevar Rajasekaran, Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms, 2nd Edition, Universities Press.
A. V. Aho, J. E. Hopcroft and J. D. Ullman, The Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms, Addison Wesley.
referenceBooks: Anany Levitin, Introduction to the Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Pearson.
Michael T. Goodrich and Roberto Tamassia, Algorithm Design and Applications, Wiley.
Steven S. Skiena, The Algorithm Design Manual, Springer.
